breaking.headline: S&P 500 heads for seventh straight loss; Nasdaq briefly negative for 2026
breaking.fact: The S&P 500 was down about 1.9% Friday morning, on track for a seventh straight loss and its worst week since April 2025, while the Nasdaq fell more than 3% and briefly slipped into negative territory for 2026; the Dow held near flat. Chip stocks sank again, with Nvidia down about 6-7% and AMD down 10%.

breaking.headline: Anthropic sinks about 12% in second day of trading after record debut
breaking.fact: Anthropic shares fell more than 10% Friday morning, trading near $85 after closing their debut at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price; the stock had opened Thursday at $111.50 and touched $115.10 before paring gains.

breaking.headline: Global stocks retreat as AI trade unwinds; S&P hits 6.5-month low
breaking.fact: The S&P 500 fell to a 6.5-month low and the Nasdaq 100 to a 7-month low Friday as investors liquidated AI-linked stocks worldwide; MSCI's world index fell for a seventh straight session, its longest losing streak since 2023.

breaking.headline: Asian shares head for worst week since 2020 as AI rout spreads
breaking.fact: Asian shares tumbled Friday, with Japan's Nikkei down more than 5% and South Korea's Kospi down 5.2%, putting the region on course for its worst week since the COVID pandemic in March 2020; Europe's STOXX 600 fell 1.5%, down 5% from its November 12 record.

weekInBrief.headline: Nvidia extends losing streak to six sessions as AI rout deepens
weekInBrief.body: Nvidia shares fell again Friday, a sixth straight losing session, after closing Thursday down 3.3%; the chip giant has lost more than a quarter of its value in two weeks as investors weigh Jensen Huang's departure and the AI spending outlook, even after a blowout earnings report earlier in the week.

weekInBrief.headline: October jobs report beats expectations, but long-term joblessness hits five-year high
weekInBrief.body: Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly triple the roughly 59,000 economists expected, and unemployment slipped to 4.1%, but the average stretch of unemployment jumped to 27.1 weeks — the longest outside the pandemic since 2016 — with nearly 2 million people out of work for more than six months.

weekInBrief.headline: Fed rate-hike odds hit 97% as gold slides to a 14-month low
weekInBrief.body: Gold slipped below $3,650 an ounce to a 14-month low as traders raised the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike to 97.3%, with the 10-year Treasury yield near 5% and the dollar firming; WTI crude steadied near $82.75 as Hormuz supply risks offset an inventory surplus.

weekInBrief.headline: AMD slides on China export-control and financing concerns
weekInBrief.body: Shares of AMD plunged nearly 8% in a single session this week on concerns over China export controls and financing practices, adding to the chip sector's rout; AMD had already fallen 7.7% on Thursday as the AI selloff spread through semiconductors.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: A projectile struck a tanker's engine room about 6 nautical miles north of Khasab at 16:45 UTC on Wednesday, November 18 — the third strike near Khasab since November 16, with the crew reported safe, according to UKMTO via Windward. Windward also found five LNG carriers left the strait with their transponders off in the week to November 17, against as few as two in AIS-only counts. President Trump said he is in no hurry to decide on Iran and will see what happens after January 1. Iranian media claimed three tankers struck mines on November 19, a claim that has not been independently verified. On oil, a small amount of Iranian crude is moving again — about 200,000 barrels changed hands ship-to-ship on Tuesday, the first such movement since July — but it has not left the Gulf as an export, while about 8.3 million barrels a day of oil and products, effectively all non-Iranian with Iranian exports near a standstill, kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11, about 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: Voyager 1 phones home from one light-day away
space.body: NASA's Voyager 1 has phoned home from one light-day away — humanity's first emissary to cross that threshold in interstellar space. Flight controllers received the spacecraft's call Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent, confirming the milestone reached November 18 at 10:16:07 UTC, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977. The data stream briefly halted over the weekend, but the carrier signal stayed strong and flight-path calculations confirmed the distance of more than 16 billion miles.

space.headline: Venus-like conditions reveal how minerals could preserve traces of ancient water
space.body: Experiments in NASA Glenn's extreme-environment chamber exposed six rock-forming minerals to simulated Venus surface conditions for 60 days and found hydrogen fluoride in the atmosphere can transform water-bearing minerals into fluorine-bearing micas that stay stable under Venus' intense heat and pressure — a possible mineralogical clue to the planet's ancient water. The findings give NASA's DAVINCI and VERITAS missions and ESA's EnVision specific targets to look for.

space.headline: Low-viscosity lavas reveal a key to Mars's past
space.body: A new study in Communications Earth & Environment uses Perseverance rover geochemistry to show the nearly 4-billion-year-old Séïtah formation in Jezero Crater formed from a low-viscosity lava lake that flowed about 200 kilometres from its vent — explaining the large interlocking olivine crystals the rover found and sharpening the picture of Mars' early geology and its capacity to host ancient life.

space.headline: Space travel changes the brain's immune cells, but not behavior
space.body: University of Rochester researchers exposed mice to simulated galactic cosmic radiation at NASA's Space Radiation Laboratory and found single-cell sequencing of nearly 16,000 microglia showed clear molecular changes — and different responses in male and female brains — yet no widespread inflammation and no measurable behavioral or cognitive impairment, a reassuring result for long-duration Moon and Mars missions.

apod.title: The Stormy Southwest Pacific
apod.credit: Lauren Dauphin, using MODIS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE and GIBS/Worldview — NASA Earth Observatory Image of the Day, November 20, 2026
apod.explanation: Tropical Cyclone Xavier, captured by the MODIS instrument on NASA's Aqua satellite on November 17, 2026, became one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the Southwest Pacific has seen in decades, peaking at 220 km/h (140 mph) — the strongest November storm east of the international date line on record. The system damaged homes and cut power in the northern Cook Islands before weakening as it pushed west; Fiji's seasonal outlook projects 11 to 15 named cyclones in the region this season.
